<20% passive investment (IFRS 9) · 20–50% significant influence → equity method (IAS 28) · joint control → JV: equity method, joint operation: proportionate · control (>50% presumed) → full consolidation (IFRS 10, IFRS 3).
Power over relevant activities + exposure to variable returns + ability to use power. Possible with <50% (agreements, board, double voting rights) and even with 0% (structured entities).
a) PPA: valuation differences & goodwill · b) 100% of assets, liabilities, income, expenses · c) eliminate investment vs subsidiary equity and intra-group transactions · d) identify NCI.

Purchase price − fair value of identifiable net assets acquired (× % acquired). Contains synergies, workforce, market position. No amortisation; annual impairment test; never reversed. Negative goodwill → immediate gain.
Identifiable: PP&E, patents, brands, customer lists, R&D projects, debt – at fair value. Goodwill: know-how of employees (assembled workforce), expected synergies.
Sum of all assets/liabilities (subsidiary at fair value) + goodwill − investment in subsidiary. Equity = parent's equity only (+ NCI if <100%).
Minority shareholders' share in a subsidiary's net assets and income. Presented in consolidated equity, separately. Example 60%: NCI = 40% × equity; NI split group / NCI.
Parent NI + 100% of subsidiary post-acquisition NI (adjusted, e.g. impairment of valuation differences) → split into group share and NCI.

Cost + share of post-acquisition changes in equity (profit − dividends). One line in BS ('investments in associates'), one line in IS ('share of profit of associates'). No NCI, no line-by-line integration.

Same as the asset they belong to: depreciation of higher PP&E values, impairment test for brands, use of provisions. Reversal of brand impairment allowed (up to original value); goodwill impairment never reversed.
